newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT -Stg/mark prepares for push up to 2.8335.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT -Stg/mark prepares for push up to 2.8335.

text.p: Sterling's prospects against the mark have turned more bullish after it poked above 2.8200 marks on Thursday, and it will try to establish a base around that level for today, technical analysts said.
After that, sterling/mark is likely to make another attempt at the peak of 2.8335, its highest level since August 1992 which it reached earlier this month, they said.

"I think it's going to consolidate today, and then move back to test the 2.8280 level, and then possibly 2.8335... Those are the key levels to watch on the upside," said Alan Dunne, technical analyst at Bank of America.
Sterling/mark was at 2.8145/50 at 0745 GMT against 2.8235/45 in late European trade on Thursday.
"Technically sterling/mark looks good, if we break out of 2.8335 we should see a quick move towards 2.85," Dunne said.

Rising above this week's high of 2.8175 on Thursday had given impetus to sterling/mark, but a sustained break back below that level will pave the way to initial support at 2.8130 and then last week's low of 2.8080-90, analysts said.
Some saw danger signals in the shape of a possible double-top formation, with its peaks at the May 6 high of 2.8330 marks and the 2.8331 level seen on June 4.
Cable, meanwhile, will remain capped but should be supported around its recent lows of $1.6210.

"The outlook remains bearish as long as it trades below $1.6432. Failure to break this level followed by a decline below $1.6300 suggests a test of $1.6210, the low traded in early June," Chase Investment Bank's technical team said.

The $1.6430 level is a congestion area that has been capping cable since late last month. But before trying that level, cable must clear an trendline resistance at $1.6390. Cable was at $1.6290/95 at 0805 GMT against $1.6345/55 on Thursday.
